'''''Viola arvensis''''' is a species of [[Viola (plant)|violet]] known by the common name '''field pansy'''. It is native to Europe, western Asia, and North Africa, and it is known on other continents as an [[introduced species]] and a [[weed]] of disturbed and cultivated areas.

''Viola arvensis'' was shown to contain [[cyclotides]], a class of [[peptides]] found in plants. The peptide cycloviolacin O2 in particular has shown to possess [[cytotoxic]] activity against human cancer cells and is therefore looked at as a potential drug lead.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://mct.aacrjournals.org/content/1/6/365.full.pdf|title=Cyclotides: A Novel Type of Cytotoxic Agents|author=Lindholm|display-authors=etal|year=2002|journal=[[Molecular Cancer Therapeutics]]|publisher=[[American Association for Cancer Research]]|volume=1|issue=6|pages=365–369|pmid=12477048}}</ref>

==Description==
It is an [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[annual plant]] with serrated leaves, and usually flowers with white all over, except the bottom [[petal]] (Although there are actually flowers with a tinge of purple at the top) and [[Dehiscence (botany)|dehiscent]] [[Capsule (botany)|capsules]]. It reproduces by seed. It grows {{Convert|20|cm|sp=us}} tall.
